geometry.locator: Double Chooz TDR hep-ex/0606025 Sec. 2.1 and Table 3; PRD 86, 052008 (arXiv:1207.6632) Table V; OSM way 331249625 and way 331249628; IGN RGE ALTI
geometry.note: Derived from two published baselines and two OSM building centroids. Not surveyed: the lab entrance and underground layout are not published as coordinates.
geometry.quote: The far detector is located at a distance of 1114.6 ± 0.1 m from RE, and at 997.9 ± 0.1 m from RW

method: Derived: intersection of two circles on a local equirectangular plane (R = 6371008.8 m). Centres: centroids of OSM ways 331249625 (Chooz B1, 4.7890472 E 50.0895090 N) and 331249628 (Chooz-B2, 4.7912861 E 50.0898134 N), 163.3 m apart (published separations: 160 m NUCLEUS, 165 m Double Chooz 2021; 140 m in the 2006 TDR map caption). Radii: the far-detector baselines of the Double Chooz TDR, 1114.6 +/- 0.1 m and 997.9 +/- 0.1 m (Sec. 2.1, Table 3; rounded 1115 m and 998 m in arXiv:2009.05515). Assignment: the TDR labels the cores RE and RW, which does not map onto the OSM unit names unambiguously, so the shorter baseline is given to B2 because the Double Chooz PRD 86, 052008 Table V predicts more far-detector antineutrino events from B2 than from B1 (3422.4 vs 2910.9 with both reactors on; equal nominal power, flux ~ 1/L^2, so B2 is the nearer core; the distance ratio alone would give 1.25, the table gives 1.18). Mirror choice: the circles meet at two points mirrored about the B1-B2 line, [4.7983783, 50.0975486] and [4.8026591, 50.0845889]. Terrain from the IGN RGE ALTI service: the plant ground is 114.7 m and the Double Chooz TDR gives ~300 m.w.e. of 2.8 g/cm3 rock (~107 m) over the far hall; the northern solution is at 138 m a.s.l. (about 23 m above the plant, no such overburden possible) and the southern one at 239 m on a hill; the southern solution is also the one 209 m from the OSM 'Chooz A' building, as the TDR says the hall is 'close' to Chooz A. Sensitivity: the baseline of the two circle centres is only 163 m for ~1 km radii, so a 5 m error in the core separation moves the point ~25 m and a 20-30 m perpendicular offset of one core from its building centroid rotates the pair and moves it ~100-170 m; accuracy_m 200 is set accordingly.
name: Double Chooz far laboratory (derived position, ~1 km from the cores)
notes: Far-lab position is 1114.6 m from the B1 centroid and 997.9 m from the B2 centroid by construction. The two mirror solutions are [4.7983783, 50.0975486] and [4.8026591, 50.0845889] (lon, lat). IGN elevation, southern/chosen 239.4 m, northern 138.1 m, plant ground 114.7 m.

summary.plain: The old CHOOZ underground laboratory in the hill about 1 km from the Chooz B reactors, reused by Double Chooz for its far detector. The position is computed from the published distances to the two reactors, not surveyed; it is good to about 200 m.
